scenarioStory.history: Patient was lifting her 2-year-old grandchild out of a crib this morning when she felt a sudden 'pop' and sharp pain in her lower back. Pain has progressively worsened over the past hour, now 9/10, sharp and band-like across the lumbar region without radiation into the legs. She is unable to stand upright or bear weight without severe pain and has been lying on the living room floor since the onset. Denies numbness, denies loss of bowel or bladder control, denies fever.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 58-year-old female supine on the floor, rigid with guarding, reporting severe lumbar back pain that began while lifting her grandchild. She is alert, oriented, and cooperative but in visible distress. → Red flags screened, analgesia given: Crew performs a focused assessment for life-threatening causes of back pain, positions the patient for comfort, and administers weight-based IV morphine for severe pain. → Morphine given, pain improves: Following weight-based IV morphine, the patient's pain and vital signs improve. She is transported in a position of comfort with ongoing reassessment.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Severe low back pain after lifting grandchild, unable to ambulate

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 58-year-old female supine on the floor, rigid with guarding, reporting severe lumbar back pain that began while lifting her grandchild. She is alert, oriented, and cooperative but in visible distress.

scenarioEvents.name: Red flags screened, analgesia given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew performs a focused assessment for life-threatening causes of back pain, positions the patient for comfort, and administers weight-based IV morphine for severe pain.
relatedChecklist: Screen for life-threatening back pain causes: neuro deficit, unequal femoral pulses, pulsatile mass, fever
Assess pain severity using the Numeric Rating Scale (patient is >12 years old)
Position patient for comfort while preparing IV access and medication
Morphine 7 mg IV (70 kg × 0.1 mg/kg = 7 mg; max initial dose 10 mg)

scenarioEvents.name: Morphine given, pain improves
scenarioEvents.description: Following weight-based IV morphine, the patient's pain and vital signs improve. She is transported in a position of comfort with ongoing reassessment.
relatedChecklist: Reassess pain score and vital signs after morphine; monitor respiratory status
Transport in position of comfort; reassess vitals and pain en route

scenarioEvents.name: Analgesia withheld despite severe pain
scenarioEvents.description: Crew delays or withholds analgesia despite a completed red-flag screen showing isolated musculoskeletal back pain. The patient remains in severe pain, becoming increasingly distressed, tachycardic, and hypertensive.
relatedChecklist: Recognize uncontrolled pain; give morphine 7 mg IV now (70 kg × 0.1 mg/kg; max initial 10 mg)
